draft.title: Recombinant plasmids
card: A plasmid is a small, circular piece of DNA in bacteria, separate from the main chromosome. Scientists use plasmids as vectors, which carry a gene into a host cell.
The gene and the plasmid are cut with the same restriction enzyme, so their ends match. DNA ligase joins the gene into the plasmid. The result is a recombinant plasmid.
The recombinant plasmid is put into bacteria by transformation, which is the uptake of DNA by a cell. Only some cells take it up.

Plasmids often carry an antibiotic resistance gene as a marker. Bacteria grown on that antibiotic survive only if they took up the plasmid. These bacteria can then make the protein the inserted gene codes for.
draft.remember: Cut the gene and plasmid to match, join them, transform bacteria, then select the bacteria that took it up.

a.q: Why are the gene and the plasmid cut with the same restriction enzyme?
opts: So that their cut ends match and can be joined
So that the plasmid can copy itself inside bacteria
So that the bacteria can take up the DNA faster
So that the gene can be switched on in the plasmid
a.why: The same enzyme leaves matching ends on the gene and the plasmid, so ligase can join them. The enzyme does not make the plasmid copy itself or help bacteria take up DNA. Transformation is a separate step.
a.clue: Think about what ligase needs to join two pieces.

b.q: Dr Nguyen inserts a human gene into plasmids that carry an antibiotic resistance gene. She adds the plasmids to bacteria, then spreads the bacteria on agar containing that antibiotic. Why do only some bacteria grow?
opts: Only those that took up a plasmid are resistant
Only those that made the human protein are resistant
Only those with a cut chromosome are resistant
Only those that were not transformed are resistant
b.why: The resistance gene is on the plasmid, so bacteria that took it up can survive the antibiotic. The plasmid in a surviving cell may be recombinant or not, but resistance comes from having the plasmid. Making the human protein is not what protects the cell.
b.clue: Where is the resistance gene found?

a.best: So that their cut ends match and can be joined

b.best: Only those that took up a plasmid are resistant

problems.detail: "These bacteria can then make the protein the inserted gene codes for" implies every bacterium that survives the antibiotic carries the inserted gene. Some survivors take up a plasmid that closed without the gene and cannot make the protein. Why (b) says this correctly, so the card and the why disagree.
